world.setting: Contemporary learning environments and cognitive training spaces: libraries, study desks, quiet classrooms, office workstations, home kitchens, memory palace mental routes. Modern everyday professionals and students mastering mental systems.
world.register: contemporary nonfiction, cognitive self-mastery, systematic mental techniques

narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.role: the analytical voice explaining cognitive systems and memory architecture; never staged as a person
narrator.look: Off-screen explanatory voice framing mnemonic techniques, drawn as a clean neutral presence.

horsley.name: Kevin Horsley
horsley.role: the author and memory grandmaster who broke the World Memory Championship record reciting 10,000 digits of Pi
horsley.look: Kevin Horsley, a sharp man in his early 40s, athletic build, short dark hair, wearing a clean navy casual blazer over a grey t-shirt, focused and deliberate expression.

everyman.name: Everyman learner
everyman.role: a professional or everyday person struggling with information overload, forgotten names, and mental clutter
everyman.look: A professional in their mid 30s, average build, brown hair, wearing a casual crewneck sweater and dark trousers, looking intently at learning material.

student.name: Mnemonic practitioner
student.role: a student actively practicing the loci method and visualizing absurd imagery along physical routes
student.look: A young adult in their 20s, slim build, wavy dark hair, wearing a light jacket over a graphic tee, actively visualizing and gesturing with focus.

library.look: A quiet modern library with tall bookshelves, organized study desks, warm reading lamps, and calm concentration.

classroom.look: A structured lecture classroom with a clean whiteboard showing numbered diagrams and mnemonic schemas.

office.look: A contemporary desk workspace with notebook lists, a smartphone, and clean spatial organization.

room.look: A familiar living room interior used as a memory palace locus with distinct stations: doorway, sofa, coffee table, shelf.

kitchen.look: A bright home kitchen locus route: refrigerator, kitchen counter, sink, and dining table as physical peg points.

abstract.look: A minimalist mental mindspace with glowing neural pathways, geometric scaffolds, and spatial coordinate grids.

objects.why: Knowledge text and manual of memory techniques.
Written memory lists, pegs, and number systems representing external recording versus internal architectural memory.
The spark of sensory imagination and vivid visualization (SEE principle).
The mnemonic key unlocking recall along a palace route.
Total concentration and focused attention eliminating distractions.
Spaced repetition intervals and review cycles across the forgetting curve.
The Car Method peg system where vehicle compartments store items.
The digital crutch creating cognitive outsourcing and passive attention.
World Memory Championship achievement reciting 10,000 digits of Pi.

focus.name: Concentration & Attention
focus.description: The foundation of memory: eliminating mental chatter and fixing awareness onto the target information.
focus.evidence: Horsley emphasizes that concentration is not hard work but the decision to direct undivided attention without multitasking.

palace.name: The Route & Loci Architecture
palace.description: Connecting concepts to known physical locations in sequence for effortless random access and long-term retention.
palace.evidence: The ancient Roman route method turns rooms, streets, and cars into walkable memory containers.

visualization.name: Sensory Imagination (SEE Principle)
visualization.description: Transforming abstract numbers and words into exaggerated, humorous, moving sensory pictures.
visualization.evidence: Memory thrives on sensory richness, extreme exaggeration, and energetic movement rather than abstract words.

spine.title: The Myth of the Broken Brain
spine.claim: Forgetfulness is not an inherited hardware limitation, but the direct consequence of passive, divided attention.

spine.title: The SEE Engine of Imagination
spine.claim: Abstract data vanishes unless deliberately encoded into vivid, exaggerated sensory mental pictures.

spine.title: Architecting the Memory Palace
spine.claim: Spatial navigation is humanity's innate superpower; anchoring thoughts to physical locations turns recall into a walk.

spine.title: Pegs, Cars, and Sequential Mastery
spine.claim: Pre-constructed mental scaffolding provides instant, ordered access to complex lists and abstract numbers.

spine.title: Faces, Names, and Social Presence
spine.claim: Remembering another person is an act of deep respect powered by anchoring bizarre images to physical features.

spine.title: Defeating the Forgetting Curve
spine.claim: Initial encoding without systematic, spaced review is temporary; intentional repetition cements neural architecture.

spine.title: Radical Ownership of Your Mind
spine.claim: In an era of cognitive outsourcing to algorithms, a trained memory is the ultimate sanctuary of independent thinking.
